newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to push agriculture at WTO meeting.
newsitem.headline: Australia to push agriculture at WTO meeting.

text.p: Australian Trade Minister Tim Fischer said on Thursday that Australia he would place agriculture high on the agenda at the first annual World Trade Organisation (WTO) meeting in Singapore next week.
"Agriculture would be an important focus for Australia," said Fischer, who will chair a meeting of the 13-member Cairns Group of free trading farm nations ahead of the WTO gathering.
Fischer, who is also Australia's deputy prime minister, said the Cairns Group meeting would consider how best to ensure that agriculture has the right priority in the WTO meetings.
"The WTO offers better than win-win results for Australia." Fischer said in a statement.
"We have already done much to open our economy and we are now well placed to push for others to do more," he said.

Fischer said he expected the WTO meeting to achieve progress on several areas of interest to Australia, including information technology which he described as an industry already worth more than A$3 billion (US$2.4 billion) a year to Australia.

"As far as Australia is concerned, the Singapore meeting needs to deliver on two core issues; practical markets access for our exporters, and commitment to preparation for another global trade round by the end of the decade," Fischer said.
The meeting, the first grouping of world trade ministers since the Uruguay Round of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade ended in 1994, will be held from December 9 to 13.
